inspection_summary: All 2,604 Python str.splitlines() lines were inspected against the normalized text. The article is mathematically coherent and unusually rich: it proves positive-proportion real-zero freedom by combining a positivity-preserving Selberg argument-principle kernel, a deliberately gapped mollifier, averaged shifted second moments, Poisson summation, diagonal/off-diagonal separation, and residue cancellation. Formula extraction is line-wrapped and occasionally glyph-risky, but the checked prose and displayed relations recover the main mechanisms. The plan preserves all four immutable v1 units and adds 27 source-grounded depth units.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A positive-cost detector converts mean control into positive-proportion exclusion
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Design a nonnegative zero detector for which one forbidden event costs at least one, then prove the family mean is below one by translating boundary logarithms into shifted mollified moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The quantitative success is family-, kernel-, mollifier-, and parameter-specific; the source does not prove a general detector theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Kernel geometry and coefficient annihilation must be co-designed
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The kernel removes an inaccessible boundary argument at the price of exponential growth, while a deliberately long initial coefficient gap makes the mollified product close enough to one to pay that price.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source acknowledges that its taper is ad hoc and does not solve the global optimization problem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Poisson diagonal and square off-diagonal are two parts of one regular main term
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After Poisson summation, the zero frequency alone has spurious delta-poles; square nonzero frequencies supply a secondary principal term whose residues cancel them, leaving a regular tau-dependent answer.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This synthesis depends on the exact local Gauss factors and functional equations in this quadratic family.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Separate structural main terms before estimating the genuine remainder
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Local support rules should be used to identify exceptional square frequencies as main terms before applying decay and large-sieve bounds to the remaining off-diagonal mass.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The available average bound is solver-specific analytic evidence here, not a universal prescription for every trace or Poisson formula.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Symmetry heuristic explains parameter plausibility but remains outside the proof
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The rigorous detector succeeds at a numerically certified mean below one, while symplectic zero repulsion independently predicts a substantially smaller low-zero contribution and motivates transfer to other repulsive families.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The prediction assumes GRH and Katz-Sarnak density and does not validate the computed mollified contribution or its transfer.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A mollifier breakpoint turns coefficient design into boundary and derivative data
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Reorganizing the square-free coefficient pairs exposes a generic convolution lemma; splitting at the taper breakpoint then makes the short range a pole calculation and the long range an integral controlled by the taper's endpoint and derivative conditions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source evaluates one constrained polynomial family and explicitly leaves optimal mollifier selection unresolved.
